Show me the books. I will find the clause.

Mode: Extraction and termination / drift: Sideways

Level 1: The Examination

When you observe an ongoing agreement, contract, magical pact, or institutional arrangement for at least [TBD:balance — 1 minute of scene time], you may make a Soul (Investigation (Mind)) check [TBD:balance DC]. On success, the GM reveals one clause, condition, or structural weakness the agreement's parties don't know about or have forgotten. You may spend [TBD:balance — 2 Leverage] to invoke that clause in the current scene, compelling the obligated party to honor it.

Level 5: Pressure Point

When you invoke a clause via The Examination, you may add an enforcement rider: the target creature or faction takes [TBD:balance — psychic damage or OP loss] if they attempt to break the clause rather than honor it. The rider is invisible until tested. Savvy targets may detect it on a Soul check [TBD:balance DC].

Level 9: Formal Correction

Once per scene, you may declare an agreement, ruling, or magical binding to be in violation of its own terms. If the GM agrees the violation is factually supportable, the agreement enters a state of formal correction: its effects are suspended for [TBD:balance — 1 hour / until resolved], and the obligated parties must negotiate a correction or accept termination.

Level 13: Termination Of Standing

You may formally terminate a contract, institution, or ongoing magical binding that has become structurally broken. The process takes [TBD:balance — 10 minutes of uninterrupted action] and [TBD:balance — 10 Leverage]. The target ends: contracts become void, institutions dissolve their formal authority, magical bindings unbind. This is a capital-T Termination and is recognized as legitimate by the setting's political and metaphysical systems. Informal agreements are immune; only structured bindings can be Terminated. Once per session.

Level 17: The Final Audit (Capstone)

Once per campaign, you may declare a Final Audit against a major faction, institution, or long-standing political arrangement. Over the course of one full session of investigation and procedural action, you examine every ongoing obligation, clause, and structural dependency of the target. At session end, you either (a) declare the target structurally sound and grant it [TBD:balance — a session-length stability bonus], or (b) identify [TBD:balance — 3] enforceable structural failures that may be prosecuted individually or collectively. If collective, the target is subject to formal dissolution proceedings.
